stimuli.first_sentence: Dr
stimuli.context: Dr. Steinberg conducted a study to learn whether adding sensory experiences during a scary movie makes the experience more frightening for viewers. In the experiment, a scary movie was shown to two different groups in two different theaters in the same building. Dr. Steinberg flipped a coin to assign participants either to a theater that provided a standard movie experience or to a theater in which hidden machines sprayed water and blew cold air on participants as they watched the movie. Each participant was asked to rate how scary the movie was using a scale of 1 to 10, with higher ratings indicating a more frightening experience.

stimuli.context: A researcher asks a sample of elementary school children to complete a survey that assesses emotional instability in relation to attachment styles. She administers the test to a randomly selected sample of those students. She then calculates the mean scores for the odd-numbered questions and the even-numbered questions separately. Dr. May then compares the two means.

When analyzing his data, he was pleased to find that this approach worked especially well for his students who had been diagnosed with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). stimuli.context: A school psychologist conducted a study to examine whether students would use an anonymous calling system to report a rule-breaking activity they witnessed on campus. Participants were debriefed after the study was completed.

stimuli.context: A psychologist knows that his client, Dan, has an obsession with numbers and tends to count things most people do not. stimuli.context: Aubree, a college student, is hired as a server at a restaurant. Members of the group were interviewed by Dr. Pilkington individually and asked to describe their most common sources of stress throughout the school year. Responses were coded and ranked according to the most frequently cited source of stress. Primary Sources of Stress 1. Difficulty using new technology in the classroom 2. Lack of time to take care of personal needs (e.g., going to the bathroom, eating lunch)
